name: dock-woman
framing: One full-length figure sitting on the ground with her legs folded to one side, seen from the side in a three-quarter view facing right, her right arm reaching straight forward at chest height, the wrist held level as if locked into something just out of frame. Even, soft, frontal lighting with no cast shadows, no rim light and no glow halos. Transparent background, the whole figure in frame with a little space around it, no ground, no objects, no text, no border.
prompt: A woman in her thirties at a street feeding machine: wire-thin and sickly, sallow skin stretched over the bones, lank greasy hair, her head hanging down, eyes half closed. Like everyone, she wears a partial helmet over her left eye: a heavy, grey, steampunk-like device of riveted metal plates and a round lens. A stained, shapeless grey slip dress hanging off her shoulders, bare dirty feet.
concierge: The Concierge's version of her: a healthy, well-dressed woman in an elegant long red evening dress with long sleeves, her hair neatly styled, smiling politely at nothing in particular, sitting gracefully as if dining at a fine restaurant with her wrist resting on the table. The partial helmet over her left eye is a smooth, seamless white shell with a soft blue light. Same pose.
